headline: High: firecrawl’s broad network/API access can leak or mis-handle sensitive web content, while LightZero is effectively non-interactive and blocks most pairwise attack paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests and transforms web content and exposes MCP-compatible client support, so malicious page text could be carried into its outputs. LightZero has no filesystem, network, or MCP surfaces, so there is no direct automated bridge; only manual copy/paste or external orchestration would make injection relevant.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is manually pasted into another agent’s prompt, injection becomes plausible.
IF an external orchestrator forwards Firecrawl text into LightZero prompts, the pathway opens.
mitigations: Strip instructions from scraped text before reuse.
Use a fixed schema for Firecrawl outputs.
Do not paste raw web content into downstream prompts.
Add a provenance tag to all Firecrawl-derived text.
requires-engineering: insert an instruction-filtering proxy between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl touches web content, screenshots, structured data, and API keys, and has broad network egress; if it processes sensitive material, exfiltration risk exists. LightZero touches no data classes and has no egress, so it is not a leakage source, but the pair still creates a one-way exposure path through Firecrawl’s outbound APIs.
conditions: IF sensitive screenshots or API keys are sent through Firecrawl, outbound leakage is possible.
IF LightZero is used as a downstream consumer of Firecrawl outputs, it does not add containment.
mitigations: Avoid sending secrets to Firecrawl.
Redact screenshots before scraping.
Restrict Firecrawl to non-sensitive domains.
Rotate any API keys exposed to scraping workflows.
requires-engineering: route Firecrawl through a DLP gateway.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Firecrawl can make network/API calls, but LightZero cannot write files, modify git, run subprocesses, or use MCP, so there is no overlapping mutable resource or write conflict. The pair lacks a shared writable surface, making capability contention provably absent from the profiles.
conditions: IF LightZero is wrapped by an external orchestrator that grants it write or network privileges, this verdict no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep LightZero unprivileged.
Do not mount shared writable directories.
Avoid granting shared OAuth scopes.
Run Firecrawl and LightZero in separate sandboxes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl can produce scraped content and structured outputs, but LightZero has no action-taking or I/O authority and no documented path to treat Firecrawl output as authoritative. The cascade is therefore limited to manual misuse or external glue, not a default automated failure mode.
conditions: IF an external workflow feeds Firecrawl output into a decision step without verification, cascading error becomes plausible.
IF LightZero is repurposed behind an orchestrator that acts on its outputs, the blast radius increases.
mitigations: Require human review of Firecrawl outputs.
Validate scraped facts against a second source.
Do not auto-act on scraped content.
Log source URLs alongside derived claims.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl explicitly touches web content, screenshots, structured data, and API keys, so compliance-sensitive data may enter a third-party API workflow; LightZero touches no data classes and has no egress, so it is not the compliance driver. The pair’s risk is Firecrawl’s handling of regulated or secret data, not a bilateral residency mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is scraped or stored in Firecrawl, retention and residency controls must be checked.
IF API keys are included in scraped pages or screenshots, secret-handling policy applies.
mitigations: Exclude regulated pages from scraping.
Mask API keys before ingestion.
Review Firecrawl retention settings.
Confirm vendor DPA and residency terms.
requires-engineering: segregate regulated workloads from Firecrawl.
